review_notes: I read the whole file. The only candidate was the private `lineHomotopy`, which is `(1 - s) • γ₀ t + s • γ₁ t`. This is the pointwise form of `AffineMap.lineMap` in a module, and the file also uses Mathlib's `segment`. I rejected it as a finding for three reasons. It is private and used only in this file, as a grep of TauCeti showed. It is a small orientation-specific abbreviation whose lemmas (`lineHomotopy_apply`, `lineHomotopy_sub`) are one-line helpers. It creates no public competing API and has no duplicated substantive API or repeated conversions. The three `windingNumber_eq_of_dist_lt_dist*` theorems are thin wrappers over the absolutely-continuous versions, so they are named specialisations rather than duplicate concepts. The other definitions and uses (`windingNumber`, `IsPiecewiseC1On`, `uIcc`, `segment`) are existing or project-internal concepts. I found no evidence of a competing Mathlib concept that justifies consolidation.
